newsitem.title: USA: Barrett dives into Gulf of Mexico projects.
newsitem.headline: Barrett dives into Gulf of Mexico projects.

text.p: Barrett Resources Inc plans to participate in the drilling of 24 wells this year in the Gulf of Mexico as the company taps into its inventory of drilling prospects there, company executives said on Monday.

Expanding beyond its traditional core areas in the Rocky Mountains and Midcontinent, Barrett expects daily net production to rise to nearly 125 million cubic feet per day equivalent (mmcfed) in the Gulf from about 15 mmcfed currently being produced from 5 wells there, the executives said at the annual Howard Weil energy conference.

The Denver-based company earmarked $113 million, or 41 percent of its 1997 capital budget, for exploration and production in the Gulf, where Barrett has been an aggressive bidder in recent federal lease rounds, President Paul Rady said.
"The real story is in our drilling of a number of prospects" in the Gulf, he said.

The company next week will reach a prospective pay zone in its High Island A545 prospect, a block off the coast of Texas that drew the most active bidding in last year's western Gulf lease sale, he said.

The company estimated risked reserves of 40 billion cubic feet equivalent (bcfe) and unrisked reserves of 100 bcfe from that block, part of the 500 bcf risked and up to 2 trillion cubic feet equivalent unrisked reserves possible from its interests in the Gulf, he said.
In its core Rocky Mountain gas plays, Barrett pegged potential reserves at between 850 and 900 bcfe, double its current proved reserves of 814 bcfe, Barrett said.
"This is one of the reasons we are excited about what we see here," he said, pointing to a three-dimensional map of one of the company's brightest prospects in the Wind River Basin in Wyoming.
